meta.title: Changelog — what shipped in MepMail
meta.description: Every recent MepMail release, newest first — what changed for you, and the day it shipped.

hero.title: What <highlight>shipped</highlight>, release by release.
hero.lead: MepMail is built in the open. Here is every recent release, newest first — what changed for you, dated the day it shipped. The raw history lives in the repository's CHANGELOG.md.
hero.note: The beta is open and self-serve: create a free account, no card required.

feed.title: Recent releases
feed.body: The six most recent releases. Older history lives in the repository changelog.

releases.title: A more useful support chat
releases.summary: The support chat assistant has a fuller knowledge base and the support page explains better what it does.

items: The assistant answers about DNS and domain verification, SMTP, API limits, creating Correio mailboxes and billing.
It makes clear Correio has no free plan and points to jean@mepmail.dev for account, billing and security.
The chat card on /support uses plainer language.

releases.title: Clearer copy on the site and in the dashboard
releases.summary: Copy and state fixes from a screen-by-screen review: what each MCP mode offers, one price format and Correio mailboxes shown as active.

items: Working Correio mailboxes show as "Active" instead of "Preparing".
The landing page says the hosted MCP has the full toolset and the local package covers the core sending tools.
The landing FAQ talks about the Free plan instead of a beta, and the pricing page copy is more direct.
Prices use one format everywhere (US$ 29), and the public menu calls the product Mail.
A broadcast refused during a protective pause shows a plain notice, without internal metrics.
The billing page shows a notice with "Try again" when it cannot load, instead of loading forever.

releases.title: One agent, several Correio mailboxes
releases.summary: One credential lets an agent work in several mailboxes: it names the mailbox per request, like "get the code in mailbox X" or "reply from mailbox Y".

items: Correio → Settings → Agents: "Connect an agent to several mailboxes" creates a credential (mmt_) for your active mailboxes, with an optional default mailbox.
On the Correio MCP every tool takes the mailbox address, and mailbox_list_accounts shows which ones are allowed.
Every mailbox keeps its own permissions, limits, send approval and activity record; a mailbox outside the credential is refused.

releases.title: Support chat on the support page
releases.summary: The /support page has a chat: the assistant answers from the published FAQ and hands over to Jean when a person is needed.

items: Support chat at mepmail.dev/support: the virtual assistant answers from MepMail's published content, in Portuguese or English.
Requests for a person, account, billing or security questions go to Jean, who carries on in the same chat.
The chat loads only when you click it and receives no data from your account.

releases.title: Support FAQ updated
releases.summary: Support page answers now reflect open Correio and the published prices.

items: The FAQ said Correio was closed and unpriced; it now explains the US$ 9.90/month per mailbox add-on on any paid Send plan.
Agents: the FAQ points to the Correio MCP for mailboxes.

releases.title: Received email closer to the original
releases.summary: Buttons, spacing and images show as the sender designed them, without giving up privacy.

items: Spacing with more than one value (like 12px 24px or 0 auto) was dropped; buttons now show at the right size.
Blocked images left empty gaps: their alt text now shows in their place.
Tracking pixels (1×1 images) are removed: they never load, even when you show images.
When you show images, background images show too, only from safe public addresses.
“Always show from …”: choose to show a domain's images automatically on this browser.

releases.title: Direct contact with the owner
releases.summary: Every page now points to jean@mepmail.dev, the MepMail owner's email.

items: Support, security, privacy, refunds and terms use jean@mepmail.dev as the contact, on MepMail's own domain.
security.txt points to that address too.

releases.title: Recipients as chips and suggested contacts
releases.summary: While writing, each address becomes a chip when you type a comma, and Correio suggests people you already use.

items: To and Cc as chips: comma, semicolon, Enter or Tab close an address; pasting a list splits it at once.
An invalid address turns red and sending asks you to fix it. Backspace brings the last chip back to edit; so does a double click.
Suggestions while you type: people you used on this browser, sent to, or heard from. No-reply senders are left out.
A “+ Cc” button next to To, easy to find.
From, To and Cc each take the full row in the composer, with room for several addresses.
Composer notices (like an address to fix) show in the footer next to the buttons, without scrolling.

releases.title: Reply all, Cc and quoting in Correio
releases.summary: Replies carry the original message quoted, you can copy more people, and phones get more room.

items: Reply all: includes everyone in To and Cc on the original, without repeating you.
A Cc field in the composer. To and Cc together allow up to 20 recipients.
A reply starts with the original message quoted below your signature.
Agents connected through the API or MCP can put recipients in Cc, and their drafts go out with the mailbox signature.
Logos and images stored in MepMail itself show at once, at the right size, without the external-images prompt.
On phones the Correio bar fits on one row, leaving more room for the list.
Reply no longer re-attaches the original message's files; only Forward carries attachments.

releases.title: Professional signatures in Correio
releases.summary: Each mailbox gets a signature with name, title, company, phone, website and logo, and email goes out formatted.

items: Signature editor in Settings → Mailboxes, with a live preview of what recipients see. A mailbox owner edits theirs; admins edit any.
Signature logo: upload PNG, JPG or WebP, and we size it for email.
Correio email goes out in two versions: formatted, with the signature, clickable links and quotes, and as text for those who don't read HTML.

releases.title: Read, archive and drag in Correio
releases.summary: The inbox gets the basics of professional email: unread mail stands out, an Archive, and dragging to folders.

items: New messages show in bold with a dot. The Inbox shows how many are unread, and so does the browser tab.
Opening a message marks it read; you can mark it unread again.
Archive folder: archive to take a message out of the Inbox without deleting it, and bring it back any time.
Drag messages to Inbox, Favorites, Archive, Spam, Trash or your folders. With several selected, they all go together.
With messages selected: archive, mark as read or unread, and move to the trash in one go.
The list keeps arrival order: starring, archiving or filing a message no longer moves it.

releases.title: A cleaner inbox
releases.summary: Correio shows more mail per screen, with readable previews and a tidy reading toolbar.

items: The list fits about twice as many emails per screen: sender and date, subject and one preview line.
Previews show the words you would read, without link and image addresses. Dates read like mail apps: the time today, “Yesterday”, the weekday, then the date.
When reading, Reply and Forward sit on the left; move to folder, favorite, spam and trash on the right. On a phone it all fits in two rows.
An open email takes the full height of the screen and scrolls once.
While subscriptions are paused, the pause notice takes the announcement's place at the top of the site, and the header badge no longer covers the menu.

releases.title: Clear rules against scams
releases.summary: The Terms of Service and the Refund Policy now spell out what happens to accounts used for scams.

items: The Terms explicitly forbid impersonating people, brands or institutions, using domains you do not control, and switching sender or account to escape blocks.
Signs of phishing or fraud lead to an immediate suspension, even before the first send: keys are revoked, domains leave sending and the queue is canceled.
Accounts suspended for abuse get no refund, not even within the 7-day guarantee.

releases.title: New sign-in and sign-up screens
releases.summary: Each access screen now says what it is for, in your language.

items: Sign-in welcomes you back; sign-up lists what you get: 100 emails a day free with no credit card, a Resend-compatible API, SMTP and MCP, and Correio inboxes for you and your agents.
The personalization illustration is drawn in the page's language instead of an English picture.
Signed in, the site header no longer overlaps its menu.

releases.title: Phone polish and legal pages fixed
releases.summary: The Terms, Privacy and Refund pages read correctly again, and the site is easier to use on a phone.

items: Accents in the Terms, Privacy and Refund pages display correctly again.
Template previews on the home page show sample text instead of raw merge fields.
The ad-measurement notice takes about a third of a phone screen instead of half, with both choices side by side.
Larger tap targets for footer links and the sign-up updates box, and more readable badges.

releases.title: Queued-sending notice
releases.summary: When the email provider pauses delivery, the dashboard says so and your mail waits in the queue.

items: A notice on every dashboard page while delivery is paused upstream: mail is still accepted and goes out on its own once delivery resumes.
Account, password and notice emails from MepMail itself keep flowing through a backup relay while delivery is paused.

releases.title: Sending protection for new accounts
releases.summary: New accounts start with a review step before they can send at volume, so one abusive sender cannot put everyone's deliverability at risk.

items: A new account sends a limited volume per day during its first days; our team reviews it once and the limit lifts. Mail past it is kept and sent after the review, never dropped.

Sending is held for review when a new account looks like phishing: imitated banks, insurers, carriers or security notices (now in French and Spanish too), sender addresses that keep changing, or a sending domain on a TLD known for abuse.
An account whose bounces or complaints cross the provider's review lines has all of its mail held, transactional included, until we review it.
When the email provider pauses sending, accepted mail waits in the queue and goes out once sending resumes, instead of failing.

releases.title: MCP on api.mepmail.dev
releases.summary: The official MCP now lives at https://api.mepmail.dev/mcp. Agents already connected on the old address keep working.

items: Connect Claude, Cursor or any MCP client at https://api.mepmail.dev/mcp, with the same OAuth sign-in on mepmail.dev.
The old api-mepmail.je4ndev.com/mcp address stays up and tokens from one work on the other: nobody has to reconnect.

releases.title: MepMail now lives on mepmail.dev
releases.summary: The API, the docs and SMTP have mepmail.dev addresses. The old ones keep working, nothing to change in your code.

items: API at https://api.mepmail.dev, docs at https://docs.mepmail.dev and SMTP at smtp.mepmail.dev (port 2587, STARTTLS).
The Mail MCP also answers at https://api.mepmail.dev/mcp/correio.
The dashboard, the site, the docs and the code samples now show the new addresses.
The je4ndev.com addresses stay up for existing integrations; the old docs redirect to the new ones. The main OAuth MCP stays at api-mepmail.je4ndev.com/mcp for now.

close.title: See the next release as it lands.
close.body: Create a free account and follow the product from the inside — the beta is open, no card required.
